About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank. 

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit. 

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

• Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.

• Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.

• Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.

• Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.

• Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.

• Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.

• Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.

• Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.

• Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.

• Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.

• Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.

• Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.

• Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.

• Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

• 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development,  quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.

• Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred. 

• Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.

• Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.

• Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.

• Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.

• Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.

• High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred qualifications:

• Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.

• Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.

• Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:

• Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.

• Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.

• Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.

• Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.

• Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

*Mercury is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., and Evolve Bank & Trust, Members FDIC.

About Teleradiology Solutions / Daignostix

Teleradiology Solutions (TRS), founded in 2002 by two Yale-trained physicians and headquartered in Ardmore, PA, provides 24x7 diagnostic radiology reporting to over 150 hospitals across 21 countries, through a network of radiologists (US, Indian certified) and technology-driven workflows.

Daignostix, the AI arm of TRS based in Whitefield, Bengaluru, builds clinical AI for medical imaging and healthcare workflows. TRS also maintains an active academic and research focus, including AI in radiology (www.radguru.net).

Role Summary:

Daignostix builds clinical AI for CT, MR, X-ray and ultrasound, with algorithms spanning neuro and stroke, pulmonary embolism, aortic pathology, urology, spine and rib fracture, solid-organ trauma and paediatric chest. Our models are used alongside radiologists (US, Indian certified), so quality is judged by clinical performance and reliability, not benchmark scores.

As a Junior AI Engineer, you will own scoped model workstreams (data, training, evaluation and error analysis) under the guidance of senior AI engineers, and support the move of validated models into production. Medical-imaging experience is welcome but not required; serious hands-on deep-learning work is.

Roles and Responsibilities:

• Model development. Train, fine-tune and evaluate CNN- and transformer-based models for classification, detection and segmentation, starting from strong baselines and running disciplined, reproducible experiments. 
• Scoped ownership. Own a defined model workstream under senior review, from dataset preparation through training, validation, documentation and hand-off. 
• Data pipelines. Build and maintain DICOM pipelines for ingestion, de-identification, series selection, pre-processing, augmentation, annotation handling and dataset versioning. 
• Evaluation and error analysis. Report clinical metrics (sensitivity, specificity, PPV/NPV, ROC-AUC/PR-AUC, per-case and per-lesion), analyse false positives and negatives by subgroup, and explain why the model fails. 
• Radiologist collaboration. Work with radiologists (US, Indian certified) to define labels, review difficult cases and turn clinical feedback into measurable model improvements. 
• Production support. Contribute to packaging validated models as tested inference services (Python, Docker, FastAPI), including unit and regression tests that confirm changes do not alter clinical outputs. Senior engineers lead serving architecture, optimisation and deployment. 

Requirements:

Must-have:

• Education. B.Tech/B.E./M.Tech/MS/M.Sc. from an IIT, IISc, IIIT, BITS Pilani or a comparably selective institution, in Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, AI, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics or a related quantitative field, with a strong academic record. 
• Experience. 2-4 years of hands-on AI/ML engineering or research experience, including deep-learning work beyond coursework, tutorials, notebooks or API wrappers. 
• Proof of building. At least one substantial computer-vision system or research contribution that you personally drove into a reproducible pipeline, service or real downstream use, and can defend in technical depth. 
• Programming. Strong Python and NumPy, and deep hands-on experience in PyTorch or TensorFlow/Keras. Able to debug data loaders, leakage, incorrect metrics and unstable training. 
• Fundamentals. Solid grounding in deep learning and computer vision (CNNs, vision transformers, detection, segmentation, transfer learning) and in statistics and experimental design (ROC/PR analysis, thresholds, calibration). 
• Engineering basics. Linux, Git, clean modular Python, Docker, pytest and basic CI/CD. 

Good-to-have:

• Medical imaging. Experience with DICOM/NIfTI, MONAI or nnU-Net. 
• Production exposure. Model serving with FastAPI, ONNX/TensorRT, and experiment tracking with MLflow or Weights & Biases. 
• LLMs and cloud. Exposure to LLMs, embeddings or RAG, and to one of AWS, Azure or GCP. These add to, but do not replace, core deep-learning skills. 

Key Skills:

Python | PyTorch | TensorFlow / Keras | NumPy | OpenCV | scikit-learn | CNNs | Vision Transformers | Detection | Segmentation | DICOM / NIfTI | Clinical Metrics | Error Analysis | Git | Linux | Docker | FastAPI | pytest | MLflow / Weights & Biases

Why Join Daignostix:

• Real clinical AI. Build models for real medical-imaging workflows and see how they affect radiologists and patients. 
• Direct access to radiologists. Work closely with subspecialist radiologists (US, Indian certified) on ground truth, difficult cases and failure analysis. 
• Mentorship with ownership. Senior technical review, dedicated on-premise GPU infrastructure, and visibility across development, deployment, clinical validation and regulatory pathways.

Founding Tech Lead (GrowthBricks)

Are you a hands-on engineer who loves zero-to-one challenges? Do you want to build systems with real context and memory that do more than reason, use tools, and drive actual business outcomes? 

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

GrowthBricks is a new project at JetMinds, backed by JetBrains, designed to give GTM teams and AI agents a shared business brain. Business context usually gets fragmented across CRMs, documents, dashboards, and people's heads. GrowthBricks brings that context together so agents and people can make decisions and execute effectively across the sales, marketing, and product stack.

About GrowthBricks

GrowthBricks is a shared business brain for GTM teams and AI agents.

It brings together the context that usually lives across CRM, docs, dashboards, tools, and people’s heads: who we sell to, why customers buy, what matters now, what we tried, and what worked. Agents and people use that context to decide what to do next and execute across the GTM stack.

GrowthBricks is a new project at JetMinds, backed by JetBrains.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on Founding Tech Lead to build GrowthBricks from zero.

You’ll work directly with the product founder and own the technical side of the product: architecture, core systems, integrations, and the agent layer.

The core challenge is turning fragmented, changing business context into reliable memory and agent actions across tools and measuring whether those actions actually drive business outcomes.

You’ll write a lot of the early code yourself, make the key technical decisions, and shape the product as we learn what works.

What you’ll work on

• Design the core architecture: business context, agents, tools, integrations, and feedback loops.

• Build agentic workflows that can reason over company context and act across CRM, sales, marketing, and product systems.

• Build context extractors from GTM team artifacts like sales calls, emails, internal documents, CRM state, marketing campaigns, etc.

• Work on prompting, context management, memory, tool use, and orchestration.

• Connect GrowthBricks to the existing GTM stack rather than rebuilding everything around it.

• Decide where to use MCP, APIs, frameworks, or third-party tools and where a custom solution is worth it.

• Prototype fast, discard weak ideas, and turn the useful ones into product primitives.

We expect that you

• Are a strong hands-on engineer who enjoys zero-to-one work.

• Have built with LLMs, agents, or agentic workflows used by real people, and improved them based on failures, evaluations, and user feedback.

• Understand how context, prompting, tools, and agent behavior fit together.

• Can design backend systems, APIs, data models, and integrations.

• Are comfortable making decisions before all the answers are known.

• Prefer simple, pragmatic solutions over unnecessary complexity.

We’re especially interested if you

• Have worked in solution engineering, sales engineering, pre-sales, or built software for GTM teams.

• Understand the modern GTM stack: CRM, enrichment, outbound, automation, and product signals.

• Have automated sales or marketing workflows, ideally with agents or LLMs.

• Have owned a technical product from a blank repo to something people actually used.

GTM experience is not mandatory, but if you already understand how sales and marketing teams work, that is a strong advantage.

What we offer

• A competitive salary and strong benefits package.

• The runway and resources of an established company, with startup-level autonomy.

• A founding role with direct influence over both product and architecture.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
 
Role Overview
Harvey’s Customer Experience team provides 24/7 support across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. As Harvey expands across customer segments and regions, the volume, location, and nature of that work will continue to change. At the same time, we are reshaping how much capacity we need and where we need it at rapid speed.
The Global CX Workforce Manager will build and own the workforce-planning function for our global support organization. You will translate customer growth and operational changes into clear forecasts, staffing plans, schedules, and investment recommendations, protecting our service-quality bar while ensuring we deploy capacity responsibly.
This is a hands-on builder role. You will establish the models, metrics, tools, and operating cadence yourself, then evolve them as the organization scales. Regional managers will continue to own their people, quality, and day-to-day execution; you will provide the global planning framework that allows those teams to operate as one connected organization.

What You’ll Do
• 
Own demand and capacity forecasts across regions, shifts, customer segments, issue types, and support channels. Translate ticket volume, active handle time, service-level targets, occupancy, shrinkage, schedule adherence, time off, and new-hire ramp into clear staffing requirements.
• 
Build and own the model that turns company trajectory into a defensible view of CX capacity, drawing on revenue and customer projections, product launches, regional expansion, and seasonality. Make that model an input to company planning rather than a downstream consumer of it.
• 
Lead weekly, monthly, and quarterly capacity reviews, clearly explaining forecast changes, coverage gaps, assumptions, and recommended actions.
• 
Establish global scheduling standards covering shift allocation, PTO, holidays, weekends, on-call coverage, and business continuity in partnership with regional managers.
• 
Create scenario plans that show when, where, and at what level Harvey should hire, cross-train, change schedules, or redeploy existing capacity. Recommend the option that best balances customer impact, employee sustainability, speed, and cost.
• 
Measure the capacity impact of AI and operational investments, including chatbot, routing improvements, provisioning automation, and evolving team responsibilities. Identify the operational changes that increase throughput or flexibility without lowering the bar for accuracy, professionalism, QA, or customer satisfaction.
• 
Support the launch and ramp of new locations and staffing models through cohort planning, readiness criteria, and post-launch performance reviews.
• 
Define consistent workforce metrics and partner with Data, Finance, People, Enablement, and GTM Operations to establish reliable reporting and dashboards.
• 
Evaluate and implement workforce-management tooling as the organization’s complexity grows.

What You Have
• 
7+ years of experience in workforce management, capacity planning, support operations, or a related discipline.
• 
Experience building or materially redesigning a workforce-planning function, not only operating within an established system.
• 
Experience supporting a 24/7, multi-region operation with asynchronous ticket-based work; experience beyond traditional voice contact-center planning is important.
• 
A track record of building useful models from incomplete or rapidly changing data and improving their accuracy over time.
• 
Strong analytical skills and hands-on fluency with spreadsheets, reporting tools, and workforce data. Experience with SQL, BI tools, Zendesk, or workforce-management platforms is strongly preferred.
• 
The judgment to distinguish a temporary coverage problem from a structural headcount need, and to recommend action before service quality deteriorates.
• 
Experience measuring how automation, AI, self-service, and workflow changes affect staffing demand and productivity.
• 
Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to drive consistent global operating practices through regional leaders without owning their teams directly.
• 
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex assumptions and tradeoffs into concise recommendations for executives.

Nice to Have
• 
Experience planning workforce capacity across enterprise, mid-market, and SMB customer segments.
• 
Experience supporting a rapidly growing SaaS or AI company where historical demand is not yet predictable.
• 
Familiarity with support quality, enablement, routing, and escalation programs in addition to core workforce management.
